questions.q: Two angles are supplementary, and one is 3 times the other. Find both angles.
questions.answer: Let the angles be $x$ and $3x$: $x+3x=180$, so $4x=180$, giving $x=45$. The angles are $45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, creating an angle of $70^\circ$. Find the measure of its alternate interior angle and its corresponding angle.
questions.answer: Alternate interior angles are equal: $70^\circ$. Corresponding angles are also equal: $70^\circ$.

sections.heading: Triangle angle sum and exterior angles

questions.q: A triangle has angles measuring $x$, $2x$, and $3x$. Find each angle.
A triangle's exterior angle at one vertex measures $115^\circ$. If one of the remote interior angles is $50^\circ$, find the other remote interior angle.
questions.answer: By the exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $115=50+x$, so $x=65^\circ$.

questions.q: Find the area of a triangle with base 14 and height 9.
Find the area of a parallelogram with base 12 and height 5.
questions.answer: Area $=\text{base}\times\text{height}=12\times5=60$.

questions.q: Find the area of a regular hexagon with side length 6, using the formula $A=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}s^2$.

sections.heading: The Pythagorean theorem and special right triangles

questions.q: A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. Find the hypotenuse.
A 45-45-90 triangle has a leg of length 8. Find the length of the hypotenuse.
questions.answer: In a 45-45-90 triangle, the hypotenuse equals $\text{leg}\times\sqrt{2}$: $8\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: A 30-60-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of 20. Find the lengths of both legs.
questions.answer: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the shorter leg is $\dfrac{\text{hypotenuse}}{2}$ and the longer leg is $\dfrac{\text{hypotenuse}}{2}\times\sqrt{3}$: shorter leg $=10$, longer leg $=10\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: Circles: area, circumference, arcs, and sectors

questions.q: Find the area and circumference of a circle with diameter 14, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Radius $=7$. Area $=\pi r^2=49\pi$. Circumference $=\pi d=14\pi$.

questions.q: Find the arc length of a $120^\circ$ sector in a circle with radius 9, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Arc length $=\dfrac{120}{360}\times2\pi(9)=\dfrac{1}{3}\times18\pi=6\pi$.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have a scale factor of $\dfrac{3}{5}$. If the smaller triangle has area 18, find the area of the larger triangle.
questions.answer: Areas of similar figures scale by the SQUARE of the linear scale factor: $\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)^2=\dfrac{25}{9}$. Larger triangle's area: $18\times\dfrac{25}{9}=50$.

sections.heading: Volume and surface area of 3D solids

questions.q: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with dimensions 5, 8, and 10.
questions.answer: Volume $=5\times8\times10=400$.

questions.q: Find the volume of a cone with radius 6 and height 10, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Volume $=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi(36)(10)=120\pi$.

questions.q: This question has two parts. A square garden has area 144 square feet. (a) Find the side length and perimeter of the garden. (b) A circular fountain with radius 3 feet is placed inside the garden. Find the remaining garden area (not covered by the fountain), in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: (a) Side length: $\sqrt{144}=12$ feet. Perimeter: $4(12)=48$ feet. (b) Fountain area: $\pi(3)^2=9\pi$. Remaining area: $144-9\pi$ square feet.

questions.q: Find the area of a trapezoid with parallel sides 8 and 14, and height 6.
An L-shaped figure is formed by a 10-by-8 rectangle with a 4-by-3 rectangle removed from one corner. Find the remaining area.
questions.answer: Large rectangle area: $10\times8=80$. Removed rectangle area: $4\times3=12$. Remaining area: $80-12=68$.

sections.heading: Chords, tangents, and inscribed angles in circles

questions.q: An inscribed angle subtends an arc of $100^\circ$. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
questions.answer: An inscribed angle is always half the arc it subtends: $\dfrac{100^\circ}{2}=50^\circ$.

questions.q: A tangent line touches a circle at point $P$. Explain the relationship between the tangent line and the radius drawn to point $P$.
questions.answer: A tangent line is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency — this is a fundamental property relating tangent lines and circles.

questions.q: State the triangle congruence criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS) that applies when two triangles share two equal angles and the included side.
questions.answer: ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) applies, since two angles and the side directly between them are all given as congruent.

questions.q: This question has two parts. A semicircular window has a diameter of 12 feet and sits atop a rectangular window of width 12 feet and height 5 feet. (a) Find the area of the semicircular portion, in terms of $\pi$. (b) Find the total area of the combined window shape.
questions.answer: (a) Radius $=6$. Semicircle area $=\dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2=\dfrac{1}{2}\pi(36)=18\pi$. (b) Rectangle area: $12\times5=60$. Total area: $60+18\pi$ square feet.
